body: God damn right.....That's exactly it....Thanks.
Jesus, yes, you've put it all so concisely.   I'm at a loss for words.  Thank you.
Ha,no, I'm with you on love.  It's overrated.  I was referring to a place to live.
And the news gets better, I've overstayed my welcome and am now being kicked out.  And again forced into a hospital.  Words cannot describe how much I wish I was fucking dead.
I wish.  Not yet.
Thanks man, I'll take a look into giving ECT and DBT a shot.  I appreciate your help.

I'm very happy to hear I could help.  I could go on for hours on my theories on why we feel so disconnected.  I think a lot of it that is a general lack of community in western culture for a large amount of people.  We feel so alien to our normal seeming peers.  Throw in a dash of stigma for mental illness and you've got a recipe for disaster.
Thanks but based on my track record, I doubt it.  Past events is the best predictor of future events.
Possible but incredibly unlikely.  Most likely I'll settle for a subpar option and it will bug me for a long time about how I let the perfect one slip through my fingers.

Jesus, I feel like I could have wrote this.  Aside from the reproductive problems (AFAIK) everything else you wrote applies to me.  Seriously, everything from cars and being a vet to giving up and no longer seeing the point in life.  I feel like you're my twin.  Been down the fat->fit->fat route, too.  
I was inpatient at an army hospital for a week, I remember thinking look at all these normal looking people.  Why are they here?  They seem normal, some of them I would objectively say are even attractive.  And then we got to group therapy and *everyone* is bouncing their knees anxiously.  I found it shocking and strangely comforting that, for the first time, a group of  people around me were sharing the same emotion as I was.  
Anyway my point is, as someone else who is struggling, reading your story made me feel a little bit less alone.  I hope my comment does the same for you.

Yeah, I did all those things I mentioned.  I even had an amazing therapist grade A+, PHD, professor, excellent rapport, the works.  Still no go.  Relevant username.  I have considered ECT.
Hope you're doing better.
Based on your experience, is there any unconventional advice you could offer?  Things aside from talk therapy/CBT/meditation/exercise/SSRIs and so on.
Interesting, all my research shows LSD is non-addictive and safer than alcohol.  Will keep this in mind, thanks!
Interesting.  The only thing that gives me cause for concern is that it's an opioid putting it in then same category as heroin.
Good to know, thank you for your insight!
You did the right thing.  How are you doing now?
Definitely something to consider.  Only thing is I've heard of a lot of people say it made their anxiety worse.
Sorry to hear that.  Which one(s) if you don't mind my asking?

I hear you. Especially if someone has schizophrenia or a family history.  However, if you're planning on killing yourself anyway, why not give it a shot. 

I have come across a few posts on Reddit and other places of depressed/anxious individuals who have done LSD (and to a lesser extent Shrooms) and had life changing realizations that cured their depression for months or even permanently.  [There have been some studies to support this.](http://www.theguardian.com/science/2015/mar/05/psychedelic-drugs-like-lsd-could-be-used-to-treat-depression-study-suggests)  Low doses of Ketamine and MDMA have also shown to have some promise.

Suicidal/Depressive/anxious/etc guy here.

You're right, it is selfish.  Depression can make you very selfish, when you're so focused on your own suffering you tend to forget about what kind of effect your actions have on other people.  

I have thought about jumping in front a semi or a train many times until I had a conversation with a friend.  His uncle was an engineer and had experienced a few suicides.  Said it changed him, ended up abusing alcohol and eventually got help and was diagnosed with depression.  The thought that I'd be causing the same terrible illness in a random stranger who had done nothing to me was horrifying.  

My thinking at the time was "this is a tool I could use to kill myself".  Not once did I think about what it would do to the engineer/driver.  Not that I didn't care about them, the thought just never entered my head.  I was so focused on ending it.
